slot.brief: Evaluate a 3×3 determinant by splitting entries into sums and using row/column operations to factor.

stem: For distinct real numbers $x,y,z$, the value of $$\begin{vmatrix}1+x&x^2&x^3\\1+y&y^2&y^3\\1+z&z^2&z^3\end{vmatrix}$$ is

verdicts.working: By linearity in the first column, the determinant is that of [1,x²,x³] plus that of [x,x²,x³]. Factoring out (y−x)(z−x)(z−y), their respective remaining factors are xy+yz+zx and xyz. Thus option (A).

working:
Split the first column: $D=\det[1,t^2,t^3]+\det[t,t^2,t^3]$, with rows $t=x,y,z$. These determinants are $(y-x)(z-x)(z-y)(xy+yz+zx)$ and $xyz(y-x)(z-x)(z-y)$, respectively.

Independent check: By linearity in the first column, the determinant is that of [1,x²,x³] plus that of [x,x²,x³]. Factoring out (y−x)(z−x)(z−y), their respective remaining factors are xy+yz+zx and xyz. Thus option (A).
solution:
By linearity in the first column, split it as $1+t$:
$$D=\begin{vmatrix}1&x^2&x^3\\1&y^2&y^3\\1&z^2&z^3\\end{vmatrix}+\begin{vmatrix}x&x^2&x^3\\y&y^2&y^3\\z&z^2&z^3\end{vmatrix}.$$
Factoring the Vandermonde product $(y-x)(z-x)(z-y)$, the two terms have remaining factors $xy+yz+zx$ and $xyz$, respectively.
Hence $D=(y-x)(z-x)(z-y)(xy+yz+zx+xyz)$.
